Deven Choksey's IPO Playbook: How to Read DRHPs, Spot Valuations, and Assess Risks

30 Oct 2026, 06:31 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily Business Desk · Source: www.business-standard.com

As initial public offerings (IPOs) continue to draw strong retail investor interest, market experts emphasize the need to look beyond short-term listing gains. Speaking at the Business Standard BFSI Insight Summit 2026, Deven Choksey, Managing Director of DRChoksey FinServ, outlined a comprehensive framework for retail investors to assess new share sales by closely studying underlying business fundamentals.

While acknowledging that many active traders view IPOs primarily as short-term opportunities—citing average trader gains of around 17 per cent—Choksey stressed that long-term investors require a rigorous analytical approach. Draft Red Herring Prospectuses (DRHPs) and Red Herring Prospectuses (RHPs), which frequently span 400 to 800 pages, provide crucial disclosures that are often overlooked due to time constraints.

Four Core Pillars of IPO Evaluation

To navigate lengthy offer documents effectively, Choksey recommended focusing on four essential areas before committing capital:

  • IPO Size: Understand the total scale of the offering.
  • Business Model: Establish exactly what the company does and how it operates.
  • Financial Performance: Review historical performance metrics.
  • Risk Factors: Examine mandatory risk disclosures to spot potential operational or regulatory red flags.

In addition to these pillars, investors are advised to evaluate the size of the addressable market and the specific industry dynamics in which the company functions.

Scrutinizing Offers for Sale (OFS) and Valuations

A central theme of Choksey’s framework involves distinguishing between fresh issues of shares and Offers for Sale (OFS), where existing shareholders liquidate their holdings. Out of 104 IPOs reviewed over a recent one-year tracking period, approximately 32 included an OFS component, contributing to a significant share of the overall capital raised.

Choksey drew a distinction between founders monetizing stakes and early-stage financial backers, such as private equity investors, exiting their positions. He cautioned that when financial investors exit at the IPO stage, they frequently stretch valuations to maximum thresholds. New retail investors entering such offerings may face severe downside risks if market valuations fail to sustain post-listing. Citing historical data from the past five years, he noted that wealth erosion totaling between ₹95,000 crore and ₹1 lakh crore was observed across five major issues featuring substantial OFS exits. He urged market participants to resist media hype and the fear of missing out (FOMO) when evaluating heavily publicized listings.

Leveraging AI and Comparing Listed Peers

While technological advancements provide new avenues for research, Choksey noted that artificial intelligence should serve as an analytical support tool rather than a replacement for human judgment. Investors can use AI tools to process lengthy documents and filter data rapidly, but framing the right questions requires prior foundational knowledge of the company's business.

Furthermore, Choksey advised against relying on a universal rule when choosing between a newly listed company and an established market competitor. Investors must identify a company's unique selling proposition (USP) and evaluate whether its business model and valuation justify buying the IPO over an already-listed peer.

Practical Implications and Verification

For market participants evaluating upcoming share sales, the insights underscore the importance of primary research over speculative trading.

  • What is confirmed: The framework relies on publicly accessible data from offer documents, official statistics regarding OFS trends, and expert commentary delivered at the Business Standard BFSI Insight Summit 2026.
  • What remains unknown: Individual stock performance, future listing premiums, and specific company valuations cannot be predicted based on general guidelines alone.
  • How to verify: Readers can review the original coverage and official statements directly through the Business Standard Report and consult primary regulatory filings available via SEBI and stock exchange portals.
